$schema: Cross-platform PII detector test fixture. Canonical source of truth.
description: Test cases that every Promptly PII detector implementation must agree on. Vendored into prompt-shields-macos-widget (Swift), prompt-shields-chrome-extension (JS), prompt-shields-safari-widget (JS), and atlas.ai/backend (Python). When this file changes, every implementation re-runs against it in CI; drift is a coordinated release.
ruleOrderInvariant: Earlier rules win on overlapping ranges. Order: email → bitcoinAddress → jwt → apiKey → iban → ipAddress → creditCard (Luhn-validated) → ssn → phone (digit-count validated) → currency → personName (bigram-filtered).

cases.notes: Empty input must produce no detections without error.

cases.text: How is the weather today in the office
cases.notes: Plain English with no PII signals.

cases.text: Reach me at jane.doe@example.com when you can
cases.notes: Canonical email address.
Plus-addressing and country TLDs must match.
US SSN canonical 3-2-4 format with dashes.
Non-dashed digit string must NOT match the SSN rule (would otherwise overlap with order numbers).
Canonical Visa test number — Luhn-valid. Must trigger creditCard before phone falls through.
Same SHAPE as a credit card but Luhn fails — must fall through to phone (which is permissive enough to match). Documents the iteration-order behaviour.
Amex 15-digit Luhn-valid format.
US phone with country code, area code, ext.
5-digit numbers must NOT match phone — digit-count validator (7-15) rejects.
21-digit numbers must NOT match phone — digit-count validator rejects.
IPv4 with octet bounds enforced (0-255).
Octets >255 must NOT match — bounded regex.
AWS access key prefix.
OpenAI sk- prefix.
Three base64 groups separated by dots.

cases.text: Account IBAN GB29NWBK60161331926819 belongs to grantee
cases.notes: UK IBAN — 2 country letters + 2 check digits + alphanumeric.
Bech32-encoded BTC address starting with bc1.
Legacy P2PKH BTC address starting with 1.

cases.text: The grant budget is €2.4M for Q3
cases.notes: EUR with M shorthand.
USD with comma separator.
NOK ISO code with M shorthand.

cases.text: I spoke with Sarah Mitchell yesterday
cases.notes: First + Last capitalised, mid-sentence.
Names at sentence start are ambiguous (could be a regular capitalised noun pair) — heuristic suppresses them. Documents the sentence-boundary lookbehind.

cases.text: Travelling to United States next week
cases.notes: Common bigram filter — 'United States' is not a person name.

cases.text: Working on Machine Learning for the project
cases.notes: Common bigram filter — technical phrases are not person names.

cases.text: Email jane@example.com about SSN 123-45-6789 and IP 10.0.0.1
cases.notes: Multiple categories in one prompt — detector must catch all, sorted by start position.
Email match claims 'jane' — personName must NOT also fire on it. Tests claimed-range deduplication.
Inputs over MAX_SCAN_LENGTH (50_000 chars) must return [] without scanning. 13000 × 4 = 52000 chars, just over the cap.
